text:
alex: FYI — rollout to prod with driverlib 12.4.3 shows a regression. small-batch gen p95 +18% (observed on canary and prod). rollout blocked.

marie: which workload? small batches only?

alex: mostly <=4 tokens continuation workloads, e2e latency jump, throughput still ok for large batches. KV-heavy chat sessions look worse.

tom: CI perf job failed earlier, I started a local bisect. initial suspect: kernel auto-selection heuristics in runtime changed in last merge.

perf-bot: perf-check/job-5421 report:
- target: model-llama-7b (quant fp16)
- infra: a100-40g
- metric: p95 latency
- baseline: 82.1ms
- head: 97.2ms (+18.3%)
- trace id: trace-0x9f2a

rachel: I profiled a sample trace — KV cache fetches look fine, but kernel dispatch shows repeated fallback to a matmul variant with higher startup cost.

alex: dumping the hot callsite from the trace:```
T=0.012s matmul_shard kernel select -> variant=matmul_tiled_v2 flags=SM80
T=0.015s matmul_shard kernel select -> variant=matmul_tiled_v1 flags=SM80
T=0.018s matmul_shard launch -> kernel_id=0x7f4d time=1.9ms
T=0.021s matmul_shard launch -> kernel_id=0x3a2b time=3.6ms
pattern: short runs choose v1 which has lower throughput for short seqs
```

marie: interesting — commit 9c3f4b8 changed the kernel scoring function to penalize memory copies by a fixed factor. That could nudge autoselect away from our small-batch-optimized kernel.

tom: confirmed locally: checkout before 9c3f4b8 = p95 80ms, after = 96ms. Bisection points to that commit.

rachel: also saw worse L2 spill behaviour when KV cache size is >3 shards; cost model now seems to overweigh memcpy, causing kernels that do more prologue work to be chosen. small sequences pay the penalty.

alex: options: 1) revert 9c3f4b8 hotfix, 2) patch scoring rule to consider sequence-length distribution, 3) force a kernel hint for canary until we have fix.

ops: full revert will require release gating and will delay other fixes. can we do a targeted rollout change?

marie: we can push a hotfix that restores previous memcpy weight for smallbatch path only. less risky than full revert. also add a unit test for seq-length aware scoring.

perf-bot: quick mitigation: you can set RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT=prefer_smallbatch in env to force the older kernel on Dedicated pools.

alex: trying the env hint on canary now. curl to control plane:```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/rollouts/patch -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"selector":"canary","env":{"RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT":"prefer_smallbatch"}}'
```

alex: applied to canary, rerun perf-check: p95 went from 97.2ms -> 81.3ms. good signal.

tom: created PR #3127 that adjusts scoring and adds a perf-reg test to CI. request review @marie @rachel.

rachel: added a reproducer that runs short sequences with KV cache >3 shards to the perf harness.

marie: plan: hotfix scoring with narrow scope, run through canary, then roll to prod. if any risk, fallback to env hint as stopgap.

ops: prepping rollback runbook but marking as low-likelihood. keep me updated when PR merges.

alex: thanks all. tagging this thread for postmortem if we see another regression after patch. :thumbsup:
